## Continuation Wave 22 — Plan 9 — Food Preservation, Nutrition, and Kitchen Resilience

Wave 22 adds a new owner-bound layer for **food preservation, nutrition, and kitchen resilience**. It remains a documentation scaffold: the active twenty-field structure stays authoritative while these passes add playable seams, high-volume authoring, grounded callbacks, and evidence gates without creating parallel mutable state. Principal owners remain **inventory, crafting, needs, disease, shelter, greenhouse, economy, and trade owners**. Material anchors include **a crock with an orange stitch, a pan of apricots by a shaded door, a sack of sorghum beneath a shelf, and a ration ledger stamped nine times**. Observable markers include **stitch warmth, apricot firmness, sorghum dryness, ledger stamp drift, shift continuity, and recovery map**.

### Pass 232 — Orange Stitch Records

This pass proves an owner-bound slice and ends with a handoff receipt.

#### Field 1 — Authority Seam

Start with a current-source census of the owner, public command, read provider, event boundary, save section, registration point, and rollback seam. The proposed extension stays over inventory, crafting, needs, disease, shelter, greenhouse, economy, and trade owners; it does not mint a second food preservation, nutrition, and kitchen resilience ledger. Treat the visible markers stitch warmth, apricot firmness, sorghum dryness, ledger stamp drift, shift continuity, and recovery map as facts that must be published by an existing owner or explicitly rejected as unowned. Search source, data, host routes, and tests for retired names and functional duplicates. Record the premise receipt, collision list, and stop line before authoring a large bank. A row that cannot name its consumer remains a proposal and cannot be presented as integrated.

**Orange Stitch Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 2 — Player Loop

Shape a repeatable loop of notice, inspect, compare, choose, observe, and recover. The player sees stitch warmth, apricot firmness, sorghum dryness, ledger stamp drift, shift continuity, and recovery map with source age and confidence, then can verify, accept, defer, share, delegate, refuse, or return. A valid command reports the owner result, resource cost, interruption behavior, and next available action. Make the loop useful during a short visit and after a long absence. Preserve safe pause, focus return, and honest empty or stale states so a missing provider never becomes a hidden penalty. One branch should protect a routine, one should spend a scarce resource, and one should leave an explicit unknown.

**Orange Stitch Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 3 — Data Contract

Define stable snake_case identifiers, schema_version, required and optional fields, bounded ranges, references, localization keys, lifecycle values, and migration defaults. Mark every value as authored configuration, a derived projection, or durable state. A malformed row is rejected with a per-row diagnostic while neighboring evidence remains loadable. Include duplicate-ID, missing-reference, out-of-range, stale-version, and corrected-content fixtures. Keep mutable facts in the canonical owner rather than embedding them in panels, narrative text, caches, or generated summaries. A representative row must demonstrate how a crock with an orange stitch, a pan of apricots by a shaded door, a sack of sorghum beneath a shelf, and a ration ledger stamped nine times become evidence without becoming an authority.

**Orange Stitch Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 4 — State Ladder

Describe offered, inspected, accepted, active, paused, completed, failed, expired, corrected, and replay states where they apply. Separate a player choice from the event that confirms it and separate a projection from a durable result. Name the mutator, reservation, release rule, interruption path, and visible receipt at each transition. Save, reload, repeat, deliver duplicate events, and reopen the host at every boundary. Invalid or stale input converges on one owner response. If a correction arrives after completion, preserve the old evidence and append the correction rather than silently rewriting the player history.

**Orange Stitch Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 5 — Host Route

Use the existing provider, panel, route, focus order, keyboard/controller commands, refresh signal, and disposal lifecycle. Present stitch warmth, apricot firmness, sorghum dryness, ledger stamp drift, shift continuity, and recovery map with source, age, uncertainty, and a next action. Loading, empty, filtered, blocked, redacted, complete, and error states explain why the player is waiting or what can be done. Long strings wrap, focus survives refresh, and closing returns to the invoking control. Missing optional art or audio degrades to text and navigation. The host remains a projection and command surface; it does not count portions, watch shifts, tool loans, lessons, or callbacks locally.

**Orange Stitch Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 6 — Cross-System Story

Bind at least three existing domains to each major result and name publisher, consumer, freshness, consequence owner, and delayed callback. Use a crock with an orange stitch, a pan of apricots by a shaded door, a sack of sorghum beneath a shelf, and a ration ledger stamped nine times as physical evidence and stitch warmth, apricot firmness, sorghum dryness, ledger stamp drift, shift continuity, and recovery map as uncertain measures. A decision should cross a practical routine with a relationship, route, shelter, archive, expedition, economy, or map surface. Subscribers read facts and ask the owner to mutate; they never reach into a foreign ledger. When sources disagree, display the disagreement and let the player choose what evidence to trust. The resulting state must be observable in a later journal, roster, trade, location, or route decision.

**Orange Stitch Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 7 — Content and Side Quests

Author disturbances that arise from material limits rather than generic errands. Every quest supplies a discovery, interpretation, complication, competing interest, escalation, irreversible choice, consequence, delayed callback, and persistent aftermath. Give each character a practical function, contradiction, object history, pressure response, and mechanical hook. Locations need a reason to visit, distinct rule, physical history, located knowledge, hazard, changed state, and reason to return. Include quiet success, costly success, refusal, and unresolved outcomes. Rewards, costs, repeat policy, retirement condition, and content-correction behavior must be explicit and use localization keys.

**Orange Stitch Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 8 — Accessibility and Performance

Set readable copy, text scaling, contrast, non-color cues, reduced-motion behavior, sound-off alternatives, keyboard/controller parity, pagination, lazy loading, and cancellation. Test repeated refresh, long localization, empty catalogs, stale rows, redacted entries, missing references, and large record pages. State cache ownership, invalidation, allocation budget, event fan-out, first-page latency, save delta, and safe degradation. A player must be able to inspect uncertainty, refuse a command, and recover from a failed route without relying on a timer, color alone, or a single sound cue.

**Orange Stitch Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 9 — Persistence and Replay

Capture only durable owner facts through the current save-section owner and rebuild derived summaries on restore. Define old-save defaults, malformed-save refusal, checksum effects, null semantics, deletion behavior, and corrected-content migration. Pair the same seed and ordered inputs across save, reload, host reopen, duplicate event, interruption, and source correction. Stable ordering cannot use wall-clock time, process identity, locale, random GUIDs, or hash iteration. A projection reproduces exactly; a durable mutation names capture, restore, migration, and rollback. The receipt includes one fixture that exercises stitch warmth, apricot firmness, sorghum dryness, ledger stamp drift, shift continuity, and recovery map at their boundary values.

**Orange Stitch Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 10 — Verification and Rollout

Sequence premise audit, source and catalog validation, owner contract, event wiring, host route, sample content, accessibility, performance, replay, rollback, and handoff. Keep evidence focused on the smallest affected region and distinguish documentation from runtime proof. Record exact files, claimed owners, commands, observed feedback, unresolved collisions, unowned mechanics, and the stop line. Roll out one representative sample first, then expand only after consumer reachability, persistence, deterministic replay, and correction behavior pass. A large word count never promotes a proposal into integration.

**Orange Stitch Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

## Continuation Wave 23 — Plan 9 — Food Preservation, Nutrition, and Kitchen Resilience

Wave 23 adds a new owner-bound layer for **food preservation, nutrition, and kitchen resilience**. It remains a documentation scaffold: the active twenty-field structure stays authoritative while these passes add playable seams, high-volume authoring, grounded callbacks, and evidence gates without creating parallel mutable state. Principal owners remain **inventory, crafting, needs, disease, shelter, greenhouse, economy, and trade owners**. Material anchors include **a crock with a violet stitch, a pot of quinces by a shaded hearth, a sack of teff beside a post, and a ration ledger stamped ten times**. Observable markers include **stitch hue, quince firmness, teff dryness, ledger stamp drift, shift continuity, and recovery index**.

### Pass 243 — Violet Stitch Records

This pass proves an owner-bound slice and ends with a handoff receipt.

#### Field 1 — Authority Seam

Start with a current-source census of the owner, public command, read provider, event boundary, save section, registration point, and rollback seam. The proposed extension stays over inventory, crafting, needs, disease, shelter, greenhouse, economy, and trade owners; it does not mint a second food preservation, nutrition, and kitchen resilience ledger. Treat the visible markers stitch hue, quince firmness, teff dryness, ledger stamp drift, shift continuity, and recovery index as facts that must be published by an existing owner or explicitly rejected as unowned. Search source, data, host routes, and tests for retired names and functional duplicates. Record the premise receipt, collision list, and stop line before authoring a large bank. A row that cannot name its consumer remains a proposal and cannot be presented as integrated.

**Violet Stitch Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 2 — Player Loop

Shape a repeatable loop of notice, inspect, compare, choose, observe, and recover. The player sees stitch hue, quince firmness, teff dryness, ledger stamp drift, shift continuity, and recovery index with source age and confidence, then can verify, accept, defer, share, delegate, refuse, or return. A valid command reports the owner result, resource cost, interruption behavior, and next available action. Make the loop useful during a short visit and after a long absence. Wave 24 adds a new owner-bound layer for **food preservation, nutrition, and kitchen resilience**. Principal owners remain **inventory, crafting, needs, disease, shelter, greenhouse, economy, and trade owners**. Material anchors include **a crock with a silver stitch, a tray of persimmons near a cool shelf, a sack of amaranth by a hook, and a ration slate stamped eleven times**. ### Pass 254 — Silver Stitch Records

This pass proves an owner-bound slice and ends with a handoff receipt.

#### Field 1 — Authority Seam

Start with a current-source census of the owner, public command, read provider, event boundary, save section, registration point, and rollback seam. The proposed extension stays over inventory, crafting, needs, disease, shelter, greenhouse, economy, and trade owners; it does not mint a second food preservation, nutrition, and kitchen resilience ledger. ## Continuation Wave 25 — Plan 9 — Food Preservation, Nutrition, and Kitchen Resilience

Wave 25 adds a new owner-bound layer for **food preservation, nutrition, and kitchen resilience**. It remains a documentation scaffold: the active twenty-field structure stays authoritative while these passes add playable seams, high-volume authoring, grounded callbacks, and evidence gates without creating parallel mutable state. Principal owners remain **inventory, crafting, needs, disease, shelter, greenhouse, economy, and trade owners**. Material anchors include **a crock with a teal stitch, a bowl of dates by a warm lintel, a sack of einkorn under a hook, and a ration ledger stamped twelve times**. Observable markers include **stitch depth, date firmness, einkorn dryness, ledger stamp drift, shift continuity, and recovery compass**.

### Pass 265 — Teal Stitch Records

This pass proves an owner-bound slice and ends with a handoff receipt.

#### Field 1 — Authority Seam

Start with a current-source census of the owner, public command, read provider, event boundary, save section, registration point, and rollback seam. The proposed extension stays over inventory, crafting, needs, disease, shelter, greenhouse, economy, and trade owners; it does not mint a second food preservation, nutrition, and kitchen resilience ledger. Treat the visible markers stitch depth, date firmness, einkorn dryness, ledger stamp drift, shift continuity, and recovery compass as facts that must be published by an existing owner or explicitly rejected as unowned. Search source, data, host routes, and tests for retired names and functional duplicates. Record the premise receipt, collision list, and stop line before authoring a large bank. A row that cannot name its consumer remains a proposal and cannot be presented as integrated.

**Teal Stitch Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 2 — Player Loop

Shape a repeatable loop of notice, inspect, compare, choose, observe, and recover. The player sees stitch depth, date firmness, einkorn dryness, ledger stamp drift, shift continuity, and recovery compass with source age and confidence, then can verify, accept, defer, share, delegate, refuse, or return. A valid command reports the owner result, resource cost, interruption behavior, and next available action. Make the loop useful during a short visit and after a long absence. Preserve safe pause, focus return, and honest empty or stale states so a missing provider never becomes a hidden penalty. One branch should protect a routine, one should spend a scarce resource, and one should leave an explicit unknown.

**Teal Stitch Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 3 — Data Contract

Define stable snake_case identifiers, schema_version, required and optional fields, bounded ranges, references, localization keys, lifecycle values, and migration defaults. Mark every value as authored configuration, a derived projection, or durable state. A malformed row is rejected with a per-row diagnostic while neighboring evidence remains loadable. Include duplicate-ID, missing-reference, out-of-range, stale-version, and corrected-content fixtures. Keep mutable facts in the canonical owner rather than embedding them in panels, narrative text, caches, or generated summaries. A representative row must demonstrate how a crock with a teal stitch, a bowl of dates by a warm lintel, a sack of einkorn under a hook, and a ration ledger stamped twelve times become evidence without becoming an authority.

**Teal Stitch Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 4 — State Ladder

Describe offered, inspected, accepted, active, paused, completed, failed, expired, corrected, and replay states where they apply. Separate a player choice from the event that confirms it and separate a projection from a durable result. Name the mutator, reservation, release rule, interruption path, and visible receipt at each transition. Save, reload, repeat, deliver duplicate events, and reopen the host at every boundary. Invalid or stale input converges on one owner response. If a correction arrives after completion, preserve the old evidence and append the correction rather than silently rewriting the player history.

**Teal Stitch Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 5 — Host Route

Use the existing provider, panel, route, focus order, keyboard/controller commands, refresh signal, and disposal lifecycle. Present stitch depth, date firmness, einkorn dryness, ledger stamp drift, shift continuity, and recovery compass with source, age, uncertainty, and a next action. Loading, empty, filtered, blocked, redacted, complete, and error states explain why the player is waiting or what can be done. Long strings wrap, focus survives refresh, and closing returns to the invoking control. Missing optional art or audio degrades to text and navigation. The host remains a projection and command surface; it does not count portions, watch shifts, tool loans, lessons, or callbacks locally.

**Teal Stitch Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 6 — Cross-System Story

Bind at least three existing domains to each major result and name publisher, consumer, freshness, consequence owner, and delayed callback. Use a crock with a teal stitch, a bowl of dates by a warm lintel, a sack of einkorn under a hook, and a ration ledger stamped twelve times as physical evidence and stitch depth, date firmness, einkorn dryness, ledger stamp drift, shift continuity, and recovery compass as uncertain measures. A decision should cross a practical routine with a relationship, route, shelter, archive, expedition, economy, or map surface. Subscribers read facts and ask the owner to mutate; they never reach into a foreign ledger. When sources disagree, display the disagreement and let the player choose what evidence to trust. The resulting state must be observable in a later journal, roster, trade, location, or route decision.

**Teal Stitch Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 7 — Content and Side Quests

Author disturbances that arise from material limits rather than generic errands. Every quest supplies a discovery, interpretation, complication, competing interest, escalation, irreversible choice, consequence, delayed callback, and persistent aftermath. Give each character a practical function, contradiction, object history, pressure response, and mechanical hook. Locations need a reason to visit, distinct rule, physical history, located knowledge, hazard, changed state, and reason to return. Include quiet success, costly success, refusal, and unresolved outcomes. Rewards, costs, repeat policy, retirement condition, and content-correction behavior must be explicit and use localization keys.

**Teal Stitch Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 8 — Accessibility and Performance

Set readable copy, text scaling, contrast, non-color cues, reduced-motion behavior, sound-off alternatives, keyboard/controller parity, pagination, lazy loading, and cancellation. Test repeated refresh, long localization, empty catalogs, stale rows, redacted entries, missing references, and large record pages. State cache ownership, invalidation, allocation budget, event fan-out, first-page latency, save delta, and safe degradation. A player must be able to inspect uncertainty, refuse a command, and recover from a failed route without relying on a timer, color alone, or a single sound cue.

**Teal Stitch Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 9 — Persistence and Replay

Capture only durable owner facts through the current save-section owner and rebuild derived summaries on restore. Define old-save defaults, malformed-save refusal, checksum effects, null semantics, deletion behavior, and corrected-content migration. Pair the same seed and ordered inputs across save, reload, host reopen, duplicate event, interruption, and source correction. Stable ordering cannot use wall-clock time, process identity, locale, random GUIDs, or hash iteration. A projection reproduces exactly; a durable mutation names capture, restore, migration, and rollback. The receipt includes one fixture that exercises stitch depth, date firmness, einkorn dryness, ledger stamp drift, shift continuity, and recovery compass at their boundary values.

**Teal Stitch Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 10 — Verification and Rollout

Sequence premise audit, source and catalog validation, owner contract, event wiring, host route, sample content, accessibility, performance, replay, rollback, and handoff. Keep evidence focused on the smallest affected region and distinguish documentation from runtime proof. Record exact files, claimed owners, commands, observed feedback, unresolved collisions, unowned mechanics, and the stop line. Roll out one representative sample first, then expand only after consumer reachability, persistence, deterministic replay, and correction behavior pass. A large word count never promotes a proposal into integration.

**Teal Stitch Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

## Continuation Wave 28 — Plan 9 — Food Preservation, Nutrition, and Kitchen Resilience

Wave 26 adds a new owner-bound layer for **food preservation, nutrition, and kitchen resilience**. It remains a documentation scaffold: the active twenty-field structure stays authoritative while these passes add playable seams, high-volume authoring, grounded callbacks, and evidence gates without creating parallel mutable state. Principal owners remain **inventory, crafting, needs, disease, shelter, greenhouse, economy, and trade owners**. Material anchors include **a crock of pears under a linen hood, a mortar with a blue chip, a smokehouse hook bent inward, and a tally strip pinned by reed**. Observable markers include **pear blush, mortar grit, hook load, tally age, hunger variance, and salvage route**.

### Pass 298 — Pear Blush Records

This pass proves an owner-bound slice and ends with a handoff receipt.

#### Field 1 — Authority Seam

Start with a current-source census of the owner, public command, read provider, event boundary, save section, registration point, and rollback seam. The proposed extension stays over inventory, crafting, needs, disease, shelter, greenhouse, economy, and trade owners; it does not mint a second food preservation, nutrition, and kitchen resilience ledger. Treat the visible markers pear blush, mortar grit, hook load, tally age, hunger variance, and salvage route as facts that must be published by an existing owner or explicitly rejected as unowned. Search source, data, host routes, and tests for retired names and functional duplicates. Record the premise receipt, collision list, and stop line before authoring a large bank. A row that cannot name its consumer remains a proposal and cannot be presented as integrated.

**Pear Blush Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 2 — Player Loop

Shape a repeatable loop of notice, inspect, compare, choose, observe, and recover. The player sees pear blush, mortar grit, hook load, tally age, hunger variance, and salvage route with source age and confidence, then can verify, accept, defer, share, delegate, refuse, or return. A valid command reports the owner result, resource cost, interruption behavior, and next available action. Make the loop useful during a short visit and after a long absence. Preserve safe pause, focus return, and honest empty or stale states so a missing provider never becomes a hidden penalty. One branch should protect a routine, one should spend a scarce resource, and one should leave an explicit unknown.

**Pear Blush Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 3 — Data Contract

Define stable snake_case identifiers, schema_version, required and optional fields, bounded ranges, references, localization keys, lifecycle values, and migration defaults. Mark every value as authored configuration, a derived projection, or durable state. A malformed row is rejected with a per-row diagnostic while neighboring evidence remains loadable. Include duplicate-ID, missing-reference, out-of-range, stale-version, and corrected-content fixtures. Keep mutable facts in the canonical owner rather than embedding them in panels, narrative text, caches, or generated summaries. A representative row must demonstrate how a crock of pears under a linen hood, a mortar with a blue chip, a smokehouse hook bent inward, and a tally strip pinned by reed become evidence without becoming an authority.

**Pear Blush Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 4 — State Ladder

Describe offered, inspected, accepted, active, paused, completed, failed, expired, corrected, and replay states where they apply. Separate a player choice from the event that confirms it and separate a projection from a durable result. Name the mutator, reservation, release rule, interruption path, and visible receipt at each transition. Save, reload, repeat, deliver duplicate events, and reopen the host at every boundary. Invalid or stale input converges on one owner response. If a correction arrives after completion, preserve the old evidence and append the correction rather than silently rewriting the player history.

**Pear Blush Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 5 — Host Route

Use the existing provider, panel, route, focus order, keyboard/controller commands, refresh signal, and disposal lifecycle. Present pear blush, mortar grit, hook load, tally age, hunger variance, and salvage route with source, age, uncertainty, and a next action. Loading, empty, filtered, blocked, redacted, complete, and error states explain why the player is waiting or what can be done. Long strings wrap, focus survives refresh, and closing returns to the invoking control. Missing optional art or audio degrades to text and navigation. The host remains a projection and command surface; it does not count portions, watch shifts, tool loans, lessons, or callbacks locally.

**Pear Blush Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 6 — Cross-System Story

Bind at least three existing domains to each major result and name publisher, consumer, freshness, consequence owner, and delayed callback. Use a crock of pears under a linen hood, a mortar with a blue chip, a smokehouse hook bent inward, and a tally strip pinned by reed as physical evidence and pear blush, mortar grit, hook load, tally age, hunger variance, and salvage route as uncertain measures. A decision should cross a practical routine with a relationship, route, shelter, archive, expedition, economy, or map surface. Subscribers read facts and ask the owner to mutate; they never reach into a foreign ledger. When sources disagree, display the disagreement and let the player choose what evidence to trust. The resulting state must be observable in a later journal, roster, trade, location, or route decision.

**Pear Blush Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 7 — Content and Side Quests

Author disturbances that arise from material limits rather than generic errands. Every quest supplies a discovery, interpretation, complication, competing interest, escalation, irreversible choice, consequence, delayed callback, and persistent aftermath. Give each character a practical function, contradiction, object history, pressure response, and mechanical hook. Locations need a reason to visit, distinct rule, physical history, located knowledge, hazard, changed state, and reason to return. Include quiet success, costly success, refusal, and unresolved outcomes. Rewards, costs, repeat policy, retirement condition, and content-correction behavior must be explicit and use localization keys.

**Pear Blush Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 8 — Accessibility and Performance

Set readable copy, text scaling, contrast, non-color cues, reduced-motion behavior, sound-off alternatives, keyboard/controller parity, pagination, lazy loading, and cancellation. Test repeated refresh, long localization, empty catalogs, stale rows, redacted entries, missing references, and large record pages. State cache ownership, invalidation, allocation budget, event fan-out, first-page latency, save delta, and safe degradation. A player must be able to inspect uncertainty, refuse a command, and recover from a failed route without relying on a timer, color alone, or a single sound cue.

**Pear Blush Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 9 — Persistence and Replay

Capture only durable owner facts through the current save-section owner and rebuild derived summaries on restore. Define old-save defaults, malformed-save refusal, checksum effects, null semantics, deletion behavior, and corrected-content migration. Pair the same seed and ordered inputs across save, reload, host reopen, duplicate event, interruption, and source correction. Stable ordering cannot use wall-clock time, process identity, locale, random GUIDs, or hash iteration. A projection reproduces exactly; a durable mutation names capture, restore, migration, and rollback. The receipt includes one fixture that exercises pear blush, mortar grit, hook load, tally age, hunger variance, and salvage route at their boundary values.

**Pear Blush Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 10 — Verification and Rollout

Sequence premise audit, source and catalog validation, owner contract, event wiring, host route, sample content, accessibility, performance, replay, rollback, and handoff. Keep evidence focused on the smallest affected region and distinguish documentation from runtime proof. Record exact files, claimed owners, commands, observed feedback, unresolved collisions, unowned mechanics, and the stop line. Roll out one representative sample first, then expand only after consumer reachability, persistence, deterministic replay, and correction behavior pass. A large word count never promotes a proposal into integration.

**Pear Blush Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

## Continuation Wave 31 — Plan 9 — Food Preservation, Nutrition, and Kitchen Resilience

Wave 26 adds a new owner-bound layer for **food preservation, nutrition, and kitchen resilience**. It remains a documentation scaffold: the active twenty-field structure stays authoritative while these passes add playable seams, high-volume authoring, grounded callbacks, and evidence gates without creating parallel mutable state. Principal owners remain **inventory, crafting, needs, disease, shelter, greenhouse, economy, and trade owners**. Material anchors include **a crock of apricots beneath a wool cover, a cracked stone sieve, a spoon with a brass rivet, and a harvest note tied to flax**. Observable markers include **apricot hue, sieve grit, rivet warmth, note age, mineral balance, and reserve route**.

### Pass 331 — Apricot Hue Records

This pass proves an owner-bound slice and ends with a handoff receipt.

#### Field 1 — Authority Seam

Start with a current-source census of the owner, public command, read provider, event boundary, save section, registration point, and rollback seam. The proposed extension stays over inventory, crafting, needs, disease, shelter, greenhouse, economy, and trade owners; it does not mint a second food preservation, nutrition, and kitchen resilience ledger. Treat the visible markers apricot hue, sieve grit, rivet warmth, note age, mineral balance, and reserve route as facts that must be published by an existing owner or explicitly rejected as unowned. Search source, data, host routes, and tests for retired names and functional duplicates. Record the premise receipt, collision list, and stop line before authoring a large bank. A row that cannot name its consumer remains a proposal and cannot be presented as integrated.

**Apricot Hue Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 2 — Player Loop

Shape a repeatable loop of notice, inspect, compare, choose, observe, and recover. The player sees apricot hue, sieve grit, rivet warmth, note age, mineral balance, and reserve route with source age and confidence, then can verify, accept, defer, share, delegate, refuse, or return. A valid command reports the owner result, resource cost, interruption behavior, and next available action. Make the loop useful during a short visit and after a long absence. Preserve safe pause, focus return, and honest empty or stale states so a missing provider never becomes a hidden penalty. One branch should protect a routine, one should spend a scarce resource, and one should leave an explicit unknown.

**Apricot Hue Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

#### Field 3 — Data Contract

Define stable snake_case identifiers, schema_version, required and optional fields, bounded ranges, references, localization keys, lifecycle values, and migration defaults. Mark every value as authored configuration, a derived projection, or durable state. A malformed row is rejected with a per-row diagnostic while neighboring evidence remains loadable. Include duplicate-ID, missing-reference, out-of-range, stale-version, and corrected-content fixtures. Keep mutable facts in the canonical owner rather than embedding them in panels, narrative text, caches, or generated summaries. A representative row must demonstrate how a crock of apricots beneath a wool cover, a cracked stone sieve, a spoon with a brass rivet, and a harvest note tied to flax become evidence without becoming an authority.

**Apricot Hue Records receipt:** source premise; owner and consumer; stable identifier; command/read route; state transition; save expectation; replay fixture; accessibility case; performance budget; side-quest hook; rollback and stop line.

Invalid or stale input converges on one owner response. ## Continuation Wave 32 — Plan 9 — Food Preservation, Nutrition, and Kitchen Resilience

Wave 26 adds a new owner-bound layer for **food preservation, nutrition, and kitchen resilience**. It remains a documentation scaffold: the active twenty-field structure stays authoritative while these passes add playable seams, high-volume authoring, grounded callbacks, and evidence gates without creating parallel mutable state. Principal owners remain **inventory, crafting, needs, disease, shelter, greenhouse, economy, and trade owners**. Material anchors include **a jar of cherries beneath bark paper, a copper strainer with one missing loop, a clay cup marked in green, and a seed ledger tied with hemp**. Observable markers include **cherry sheen, strainer gap, cup mark, ledger knot, iron intake, and pantry link**.

## Wave 35 integration closeout receipt — Plan 9: Food Preservation, Nutrition, and Kitchen Resilience

**Closeout status:** documentation-only; READY FOR PREMISE AUDIT. This receipt does not claim implementation.

**Program role:** inventory, crafting, needs, disease, shelter, greenhouse, economy, trade, and kitchen content

**Primary owners:** inventory, crafting, needs, disease, shelter, greenhouse, economy, and trade owners

**Required delta:** a preservation and nutrition projection over existing inventory, needs, spoilage, and kitchen owners, with no second food or calorie ledger

**First safe slice:** one validated preservation batch with source age, nutrition consequence, refusal path, and recovery callback

**Evidence anchors:** a crock seal, a measured portion card, a greenhouse basket, and a pantry repair note

**Observable signals:** batch age, seal confidence, nutrient balance, appetite drift, fuel cost, and recovery route

### Closeout boundary

The plan closes at the design boundary where one current owner can publish a fact, one consumer can display or consume it, one command can be issued through the owner, and one recovery path can return the player to a known state. The plan does not create a second ledger, registry, cache authority, save store, event bus, or presentation-owned counter. A row remains design-only until a current source search proves its consumer.

### Integration contract

The first receipt must identify the owner, public API, data file, save section or stateless proof, host route, focused tests, and rollback. It must exercise source age, stale input, duplicate delivery, interruption, correction, keyboard/controller parity, empty and error states, and one delayed content callback. The same seed and ordered inputs must reproduce the result across save, reload, host reopen, and duplicate event delivery.

### Content and failure gate

The first content slice uses pantry disputes, preservation lessons, greenhouse failures, meal promises, ration choices, and repair callbacks. It includes discovery, interpretation, complication, competing interest, choice, quiet success, costly success, refusal, unresolved outcome, delayed callback, repeat policy, and retirement rule. It must stop safely for duplicate spoilage state, hidden nutrition math, inventory mutation in UI, and stale batch display. Prose can describe evidence and uncertainty but cannot create a gameplay fact.

### Handoff

**MUST PRESERVE:** existing authority, engine-free Core, JSON data authority, deterministic ordering, current save ownership, truthful UI, and active path claims.

**MUST ADD:** one premise receipt, one owner-bound slice, one validator-backed sample, one replay or stateless proof, one accessible route, one focused verification result, and one rollback note.

**MUST NOT DO:** duplicate state, revive retired architecture, claim runtime integration from document volume, or widen the catalog before reachability.

**NEXT ACTION:** run the bounded premise audit for the first safe slice and return the evidence to the integrator.
